chunk_findings.detail: `git commit --no-verify` only bypasses `pre-commit` and `commit-msg`; it does **not** bypass the `prepare-commit-msg` hook. In a repository whose `prepare-commit-msg` hook is slow (for example a 120-second script), the event file is still staged in the shared index while that hook runs, because the shared index is only reset after the `commit` command returns. A normal lane committing during that window (normal commits do not take this event-only serialized lock) will sweep `.ddflow/events/<file>` into its commit, and the event commit then fails with `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`, reproducing the exact B-events-commit-races-shared-main bug this change claims to fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/eventcommit.py:196

chunk_findings.detail: The rewrite removes the parts that made the old test hit the actual regression. The old test installed a sleeping `pre-commit` hook and only started the second door after the first had entered that hook, guaranteeing overlapping commits on the old code. The new test uses a `threading.Barrier` at `K.session_end` entry and no hook, so under scheduling where one thread completes its whole `K.session_end` before the other actually runs `git commit`, the unfixed code returns two clean commits and `HEAD:{shard}` contains `"s1"` and `"s2"`, so the test passes. It also removes the old per-door assertions `out.data.get("events_committed")`, `"nothing to commit" not in note`, `first != second`, and `'"s2"' in held`. Consequently the exact bug outcome—one door’s line swept into the other’s commit while the first door reports `"nothing to commit"`—also passes, since the new loop only rejects `"cannot lock ref"` and `"index.lock"`. The regression test no longer reliably fails on B-events-commit-races-shared-main.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_eventcommit_hooks_unlocked.py:test_two_doors_committing_at_once_do_not_commit_each_others_stage

chunk_findings.detail: The monkeypatch commits `other.txt` synchronously before calling `real(root, *args, **kw)`. The foreign “landed” commit is therefore already HEAD when the event-log `git commit` process starts, so git sees the new HEAD as its parent and the commit succeeds on the first attempt; it never fails with the `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'` race. Because the race is not reproduced, `EC.commit_shards` will not emit the `"made again on top of it"` note, and the assertion `assert sha and "made again on top of it" in note` fails on the fixed code. The foreign commit must be inserted after our `git commit` has read the old HEAD but before its ref update, not before the subprocess starts.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_eventcommit_hooks_unlocked.py test_a_commit_that_lands_during_the_commit_is_not_reverted / land_during_commit

chunk_findings.detail: The test `test_a_commit_that_lands_during_the_commit_is_not_reverted` asserts `assert sha and "made again on top of it" in note`, but the mock `land_during_commit` function returns `real(root, *args, **kw)` which executes the actual `git commit` inside `EC.commit_shards`. Given input calling `EC.commit_shards(repo, "mine")`, the monkeypatched function triggers a concurrent commit during `git commit`, causing a ref lock error or non-zero exit from git, which results in `sha` being `None` and the note stating that the commit was not made again, causing the test assertion to fail with `AssertionError: None is not true`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_eventcommit_hooks_unlocked.py:182

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten race test no longer fails on the bug it names. It only checks that HEAD's shard contains both `"s1"` and `"s2"` and that notes lack `cannot lock ref` / `index.lock`. If door s1's commit sweeps the shared index (s2's staged line lands under s1's message) and s2 then records `events_note` `"nothing to commit"` with `events_committed` false, `uncommitted_shards` is empty and both strings are in `HEAD` — the assertions pass. The old checks (`events_committed` per door, distinct SHAs, `"s2"` present in s2's own commit) were removed, so this input no longer distinguishes a serialized pair of commits from the sweep the bug describes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_eventcommit_hooks_unlocked.py:test_two_doors_committing_at_once_do_not_commit_each_others_stage

chunk_findings.detail: The change to `git commit --no-verify` does not answer the previous finding: `--no-verify` skips only `pre-commit` and `commit-msg`, not `prepare-commit-msg`. In a repository whose `prepare-commit-msg` hook is slow (for example a 120-second script), the event file is still staged in the shared index while that hook runs, because the shared index is reset only after the `git commit` command returns. A normal lane committing during that window (normal commits do not take this event-only serialized lock) will sweep `.ddflow/events/<file>` into its own commit, and the event commit then hits the same `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'` race this change is supposed to eliminate.

data.probe: REFUTED (mechanism is false): the events commit stages into a PRIVATE index (git_dir/ddflow-eventcommit.index via GIT_INDEX_FILE), never the shared index, so a concurrent normal-lane commit cannot sweep the shard while any hook runs; the shared index is touched only by the git reset after the commit. The bug reported the check-msg hook (a commit-msg hook, 124s+), which --no-verify DOES skip; prepare-commit-msg is a rarer hook git offers no flag to skip, and the private index already keeps the shard out of the shared index. Regression: uv run pytest tests/test_eventcommit_hooks_unlocked.py::test_an_events_only_commit_skips_the_hooks fails on the unfixed code (commit-msg hook rejected the commit) and passes after --no-verify.
